result:
Good. That settles what it's for. The biggest open piece is how the on-call person says "I've got it." That choice decides whether the service only sends texts or also has to receive them.

- **Reply to the text** (e.g. "OK"). This is the most natural thing to do half-asleep at 3am. It needs an SMS provider that handles replies, like Twilio. The service can check that provider for replies every few seconds, so nothing in the greenhouse has to be reachable from the internet. The cost is a bit more code and a provider account with a phone number.
- **Tap a link in the text.** This is just as easy for the person. But the link has to open something, so you'd need a small web page reachable from outside your network. That means more to set up and secure.
- **No acknowledgment at all.** Texts repeat every 15 minutes until the reading is back in range. This is the simplest to build. But the person keeps getting buzzed while they're already out there fixing the heater, and nobody knows whether anyone saw the alert.

I'd go with **reply to the text**. It gives you a real "someone's on it" signal and keeps the greenhouse off the open internet.

Two smaller calls I'm making unless you say otherwise:
- Each zone gets its own safe minimum and maximum for temperature and humidity in a config file.
- The on-call roster is a simple file listing each week's person and phone number.

Which way do you want to go on acknowledgment?
